research_role: First bridge after Campo Grafico: test what Italian editorial intelligence preserves, mutates or rejects across publication identity, media, wartime constraint and postwar reconstruction.

verified_evidence.evidence: Domus began as a broad culture-of-living publication and Ponti's editorial field brought architecture, applied arts, graphics, objects and domestic life into one publication rather than treating them as isolated disciplines.
verified_evidence.transfer: An editorial system may be coherent because it has a worldview, not because every contribution belongs to one media category.

verified_evidence.evidence: Ponti worked simultaneously as architect/designer and editor, writing articles, notes, aphorisms and precise captions across decades.
verified_evidence.transfer: Editorial judgement is strongest when writing, image choice, object design and spatial composition can inform one another instead of being serial handoffs.

verified_evidence.evidence: Giorgio Casali's square negatives were frequently reframed into unpredictable rectangular prints; the resulting different image sizes required free white space in Domus layouts.
verified_evidence.transfer: Whitespace can be a consequence of image truth and editorial relation rather than a preset luxury-magazine motif.

verified_evidence.evidence: Postwar Domus rhythm used coloured strip inserts and different paper stocks; coarse pale-blue paper could signal a subject change while half-page colour films altered rhythm without stopping flow.
verified_evidence.transfer: Material, colour field and partial interruption can function as semantic punctuation.

verified_evidence.evidence: Lisa Ponti described the Domus method as a worldwide effort by affinity, with architects, designers and artists directly indicating and documenting one another's work.
verified_evidence.transfer: Contributor networks can act as distributed editorial sensing; central authority need not flatten local voices.

verified_evidence.evidence: Stile's late-war form became a modest red-black-white booklet under material scarcity while carrying ideas for intelligent, inexpensive reconstruction; Domus itself suspended publication in 1945 amid paper/distribution difficulty.
verified_evidence.transfer: Scarcity-driven visual reduction is historical constraint evidence, not an aesthetic recipe to imitate.

verified_evidence.evidence: Bruno Munari's 1944 Domus work explicitly examined historical oscillation between controlled Reason and convoluted Fantasy, while his layouts moved away from austere rigidity toward a more flexible and intuitive formula.
verified_evidence.transfer: Editorial intelligence can compose controlled and expressive states as meaningful alternation rather than choosing one permanent visual temperament.

verified_evidence.evidence: The later Pontian Atlas deliberately used Ponti as corpus/subtext for contemporary artists rather than reproducing a commemorative historical style.
verified_evidence.transfer: Historical evidence may be reactivated through new relations and contemporary interpretation without reenactment.

continuities: material and production can carry meaning
editorial form may respond to content rather than fixed template
historical/source objects should retain identity when their identity matters
mutations: Campo Grafico foregrounds publication-as-workshop and evidence; Ponti expands publication into a total cultural world of living, making and seeing.
Campo Grafico often makes production itself editorial content; Domus increasingly turns photography, material rhythm and contributor affinity into an editorial sensing system.
Ponti adds a stronger model of editor-as-maker whose writing, design, architecture and image judgement coexist.

rejection_memory: Do not learn Ponti as a decorative 1950s look.
Do not imitate Domus mastheads, covers, period furniture, colour palettes or typography as identity shortcuts.
Do not convert wartime scarcity into a minimalist style prescription.
Do not treat whitespace as automatically refined; it must have a compositional or semantic reason.
Do not force architecture-magazine neutrality: Domus history itself includes colour, energy and changing visual systems.
Do not confuse historical continuity with fixed visual sameness.
next: Feed these bridge grammars into the existing blind experimental loop while continuing the historical bridge through postwar Domus/Casabella and the 1958-1977 period. No capability promotion yet.
